title: A connected algebraic-group homomorphism is determined on a Borel subgroup
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $A,D$ be smooth connected affine $F$-group schemes of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A closed subgroup scheme means [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Let $B\subseteq A$ be a Borel subgroup: a smooth connected solvable closed subgroup maximal among such subgroups. Here solvable means that its successive scheme-theoretic commutator subgroups eventually become trivial, and a commutator subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $u,v:A\to D$ be homomorphisms of $F$-group schemes. If $u|_B=v|_B$ as scheme morphisms, then $u=v$ as scheme morphisms. Equality means equality on points over every commutative $F$-algebra. Neither reductivity nor surjectivity nor any condition on the kernels is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, printed p.358, case R=k, with its proof by descent of u(x)v(x)^{-1} to the complete flag variety A/B.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-general-borel-flag-variety], let $X=\mathcal B(A)$ and $x=b_B$. Then $X$ is nonempty, smooth, connected, proper and separated of finite type over $F$, the stabilizer of $x$ is exactly $B$, and $A(F)x=X(F)$. Let $O$ be the reduced orbit of $x$, a locally closed subscheme by [lem-sfb-smooth-group-orbit-geometry]. Every closed point of $X$ is $F$-rational by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base], so belongs to $O$. By [lem-sc-lft-over-field-jacobson-space] the closed points are dense in $X$; hence $O$ is dense. A locally closed subset is open in its closure, so $O$ is open in $X$. If its closed complement were nonempty, the same Jacobson statement applied to that complement would give a closed point of $X$ outside $O$, a contradiction. Thus $|O|=|X|$. By [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced] applied over $\operatorname{Spec}F$, $X$ is reduced. The reduced induced structure on this full open subset is therefore $X$ itself. Consequently $O=X$ as schemes, not merely on $F$-points.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358: the complete flag variety; Theorem 17.9 and Section 17f, pp.354,368--369. The orbit identification is written out using the cited orbit and Jacobson statements.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] to the action on $X$ and $x$, whose scheme stabilizer is $B$. Since its reduced orbit is $X$, this identifies $A/B$ with $X$ by $aB\mapsto ax$. Write $q:A\to X$ for the resulting orbit map. The same statement gives faithful flatness and the isomorphism $A\times_F B\xrightarrow{\sim}A\times_X A$, $(a,b)\mapsto(a,ab)$. The morphism $q$ is quasi-compact by clause (b) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], since $A\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is finite type and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is separated. Thus $\{q\}$ is an fpqc covering in [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]: for an affine open $V\subset X$, the inverse image $q^{-1}V$ is quasi-compact and has a finite affine open cover; flatness and surjectivity of $q$ give exactly the covering condition on their images.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, use of the quotient; Propositions 5.24--5.25 and Corollary 5.27, pp.104--105. Quasi-compactness is checked for the cited fpqc descent statement.

proof.text:
Using the multiplication and inverse morphisms of [def-sc-group-scheme], form $\delta:A\to D$, $\delta(a)=u(a)v(a)^{-1}$. For every commutative $F$-algebra $R$, $a\in A(R)$ and $b\in B(R)$, the hypothesis gives $u(b)=v(b)$ and hence
$$\delta(ab)=u(a)u(b)(v(a)v(b))^{-1}=u(a)u(b)v(b)^{-1}v(a)^{-1}=u(a)v(a)^{-1}=\delta(a).$$
This is the group-axiom identity of morphisms on $A\times_F B$, so under the isomorphism in step 2 the two pullbacks of $\delta$ to $A\times_X A$ agree. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to $\{q\}$ to obtain a unique scheme morphism $\bar\delta:X\to D$ with $\bar\delta q=\delta$. It is an $F$-morphism: its composite with $D\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ and the structure map of $X$ have the same pullback along $q$, so the uniqueness assertion of that same descent statement identifies them.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, first two sentences of proof; Proposition 5.21, p.104. Descent is expressed by the effective-epimorphism form of Stacks Tag 023Q.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-reduced-algclosed-global-sections-product] to $X$: properness, reducedness and connectedness were established in step 1 and $F$ is algebraically closed. There is exactly one nonempty connected component, so the structural map $\rho:F\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ is an isomorphism of $F$-algebras. Write $D\simeq\operatorname{Spec}C$, possible since $D$ is affine. The global-sections map of the $F$-morphism $\bar\delta$ is an $F$-algebra map $\theta:C\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. Set $\psi=\rho^{-1}\theta:C\to F$, and let $d:\operatorname{Spec}F\to D$ be the corresponding $F$-point. The natural bijection of [lem-a1-locally-ringed-space-affine-adjunction] says that $\bar\delta$ and $d\circ p_X$ are equal: both induce the ring map $\rho\psi=\theta$. Thus the constancy obtained here is equality of scheme morphisms, retaining nilpotent test algebras.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358; Appendix A.75(f),(g), p.583. The scheme-level constancy argument uses Stacks Tags 0BUG and 01I1 through the cited nodes.

proof.text: Evaluate $\bar\delta q=\delta$ at the identity $e_A:\operatorname{Spec}F\to A$. Since $u$ and $v$ are homomorphisms, $\delta e_A=e_D$. Since $\bar\delta=d\circ p_X$ and $p_Xq e_A=\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Spec}F}$, this gives $d=e_D$. Therefore $\delta=e_D\circ p_A$ as morphisms. The group axioms in [def-sc-group-scheme], or multiplication of this identity by $v$ on the right, now give $u=v$. In functor-of-points notation the same cancellation reads $u_R(a)v_R(a)^{-1}=1\Rightarrow u_R(a)=v_R(a)$ for every commutative $F$-algebra $R$ and every $a\in A(R)$.

source.place: Proposition 17.21, p.358, first paragraph of proof: the constant value is the identity, and the two homomorphisms agree.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 17.21, printed p.358, case R=k; quotient descent of Proposition 5.21 and constancy in Appendix A.75(f),(g).

tool_uses.why: Nullstellensatz identifies all closed points of the finite-type flag scheme as rational, needed for the routine orbit comparison; no unit-specific substitute is needed.
Density of closed points proves that the transitive flag orbit fills the flag scheme.
Smoothness over the field makes the flag scheme reduced; this is a general morphism-property tool.
Finite-type cancellation supplies quasi-compactness of the quotient map for fpqc descent.
Effective descent of morphisms descends the right-invariant difference map; this is exactly the general quotient-descent tool used by Milne.
Computes regular functions on the proper connected reduced flag scheme as F.
Naturality of the Spec/global-sections bijection turns the global-functions computation into constancy as a scheme morphism.
